subject: zoology
question_text: Define the term metabolism. Give any one example.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.50, VSAQ 69). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. BOOK WORDING: the book lists photosynthesis among its examples; photosynthesis is a metabolic reaction but is a plant process, so the card gives animal examples for a zoology paper. CROSS-BANK: botany asks the same definition in ts_ipe_b1_lw_metabolism_anabolism_catabolism with a different second half. The book prints no year citation for this question, so `appearances` is empty.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What metabolism is
steps.why: Metabolism is a total, not a single reaction, so the definition must say all the chemical reactions of the body taken together.
common_mistakes: Naming one reaction as the definition. One reaction is an example; metabolism is all of them together.
Writing that non-living things show metabolism. They do not, and this is one of the marks of a living body.
steps.memory_tip: Metabolism is the whole sum: every chemical change of the body added together.
steps.margin_note: One sentence of definition and one line on why it matters. Then the example.

steps.label: The example
steps.why: One named reaction shows that the student can point to metabolism happening, and naming a building reaction beside a breaking one shows both halves of it.
common_mistakes: Giving photosynthesis in a zoology paper. It is a metabolic reaction, but choose an animal example such as digestion or respiration.
steps.memory_tip: Anabolic builds up, catabolic breaks down; metabolism is both together.
steps.margin_note: Only one example is asked. Name two or three at most.
